title: Pakistan Solar Price Tracker: Panels, Inverters | Wattlyst
meta: Monthly tracker of solar system, panel, inverter and battery prices in Pakistan from dealer price lists, each with its source and date, and a CSV.
author: ali-ahmad

p: Installed prices include panels, inverter, structure, cables, protection and labour. An on-grid 10 kW system was listed at Rs 950,000 to Rs 1,200,000 (4 sources) and a 5 kW system at Rs 550,000 to Rs 900,000. Hybrid systems carry a battery, so their range depends on battery size more than on panel count.

Sizes backed by a single source are listed with a source count of one: treat those as a rough guide. Use the solar system price calculator to estimate any size between the listed ones and the quote checker to compare a written quote.

Panels are priced per watt: Rs 40.00 to Rs 45.50 for Tier-1 N-type modules. Hybrid inverters cost Rs 229,000 to Rs 265,500 at 6 kW and Rs 375,000 to Rs 550,000 at 10 kW. A 5 kWh lithium (LiFePO4) pack costs Rs 215,000 to Rs 310,000 and a 12 V tubular battery Rs 40,620 to Rs 72,500.
Equipment prices are retail list prices without installation. They move with the rupee, import duties and sales tax on solar equipment, which is why the tracker is dated and refreshed monthly.

Each month Wattlyst collects current price ranges from Pakistani dealer price lists, installer price guides and news reports. For a size with four or more sources the range is the median of the sources' lows and highs; with fewer sources it is the lowest low and the highest high, so a single source keeps its full range. Obvious data errors and single-figure sources are excluded and the reason is recorded. Prices are dated where the source gives a date; where it does not, the date shown is the one we could infer (for example from the page's image paths) or the day we found it, and the source list says which. Some sources date from earlier in the year rather than this month, so check each one's date in the list below.
The previous month's figures are frozen before the new month replaces them, so the CSV becomes a price history. Corrections go to the contact page.

Wattlyst Pakistan Solar Price Tracker, 2026-10-14: Tier-1 solar panels Rs 40.00 to Rs 45.50 per watt; 10 kW on-grid system Rs 950,000 to Rs 1,200,000 installed; 10 kW hybrid Rs 1,400,000 to Rs 1,800,000; 5 kWh lithium battery Rs 215,000 to Rs 310,000. Compiled from dealer and installer price lists, each with its source and date; free to quote with a link.

faq.q: What is the solar panel price per watt in Pakistan today?
faq.a: Rs 40.00 to Rs 45.50 per watt for Tier-1 N-type panels in the dealer price lists checked on 2026-10-14, about Rs 23,400 to Rs 26,618 for a 585 W panel.

faq.q: How much does a 10 kW solar system cost in Pakistan?
faq.a: About Rs 950,000 to Rs 1,200,000 installed for an on-grid system and Rs 1,400,000 to Rs 1,800,000 for a hybrid system with a battery.

faq.q: How much is a lithium battery for solar?
faq.a: A 5 kWh (51.2 V, 100 Ah) LiFePO4 pack is listed at Rs 215,000 to Rs 310,000. Compare the warranty years and cycle rating, not only the price.

faq.q: Are solar prices going up or down?
faq.a: The tracker started this month, so there is no month-on-month change yet; from next month each table shows the change. Panel prices move with the dollar rate and with any change in sales tax on solar equipment.

faq.q: Can I use these prices in an article?
faq.a: Yes, under CC BY 4.0: credit Wattlyst and link to this page. Download the CSV for every figure with its source count and date.

key_facts: A 5 kW on-grid solar system costs about Rs 550,000 to Rs 900,000 installed (Rs 110.00 to Rs 180.00 per watt) in the price lists checked on 2026-10-14.
Solar panels sell for Rs 40.00 to Rs 45.50 per watt (median of 6 dealer sources), so panels are well under half of an installed on-grid price.
A Rs 229,000 to Rs 265,500 range covers most 6 kW hybrid inverters; a 5 kWh lithium battery costs Rs 215,000 to Rs 310,000.
Smaller systems cost more per watt: Rs 100.00 to Rs 166.67 for 3 kW on-grid against Rs 95.00 to Rs 120.00 for 10 kW.

All figures are secondary-source market prices; every data point has a source link and a date, taken from the source where it gives one and marked where it does not. Wattlyst does not sell solar equipment.
